CMS Part B 2024 (drug_demand): 59,614,546 dosage units over 52,146 beneficiaries = 1,143.2 mg each, and J3111 is 'injection, romosozumab-aqqg, 1 mg'. The label caps treatment at 12 monthly 210 mg doses, so a full labelled course and a full labelled year are both 2,520 mg; a beneficiary averages 0.4537 of it and 1 - 0.4537 = 0.5463. The ratio is stable across 2020 to 2024 (0.463, 0.437, 0.447, 0.454, 0.454). Internal check: 59,614,546 mg at 210 mg a dose is 283,879 doses against 285,908 claims in the same file, within 0.7%, so a claim is a dose and a beneficiary averages 5.48 of the 12. Published cross-check: Soen S, Wang A, Hamaya E, Chien HC, Lin TC, J Bone Miner Metab 2024;42(6):653-667, doi 10.1007/s00774-024-01530-6, PMID 38987505 (Japanese claims, 13,694 romosozumab initiators across the Medical Data Vision and Japan Medical Data Center databases) reports 12-month romosozumab discontinuation of 62.4% and 58.8% in MDV and 57.1% and 52.7% in JMDC across the launch-year and second-year cohorts, which brackets the 54.6% measured here, and a mean of 9.7, 9.8, 7.3 and 7.8 injections over 12 months against the 9.96 this rate implies (1/0.5463 = 1.83 beneficiary-years at 5.44 doses each)
column12: Judgement on method, stated: romosozumab is a capped 12-month course, so a patient who completes it stops because the label says to, not because the disease resolved. The measured rate is not 1.0 because the course is monthly and straddles a calendar year end: a patient starting in July bills six doses in each of two years. That is why this is read off dosage units rather than set to 1.0, which is what the book does for a 51-week course that cannot straddle a year end. The case against: a sequential-therapy patient who moves to denosumab or a bisphosphonate after 12 doses is counted here as a stop, which is correct for this product and understates the franchise

(1) Children aged 5 to 17 are 23.18% of the prevalent pool. Lindahl K, Astrom E, Rubin CJ, Grigelioniene G, Malmgren B, Ljunggren O, Kindmark A, 'Genetic epidemiology, prevalence, and genotype-phenotype correlations in the Swedish population with osteogenesis imperfecta', Eur J Hum Genet 2015;23(8):1042-1050, doi 10.1038/ejhg.2015.81, PMID 25944380, give a point prevalence of 7.40 per 100,000 among Swedish children under 18 (142 children in a denominator of 1,919,094 at 2010-12-31). Applied to the 53,529,481 US residents aged 5 to 17 (same Census file as the pool row): 535.29481 x 7.40 = 3,961 children, which is 3,961 / 17,089 = 0.2318. (2) The severity gate is taken at 32%, the share of US paediatric osteogenesis imperfecta patients who actually receive a bone treatment: Yang EC, Cigeroglu O, Gupta RN et al., JBMR Plus 2025;9(10):ziaf124, doi 10.1093/jbmrpl/ziaf124, PMID 40978118 (IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, January 2016 to February 2020, 2,095 US osteogenesis imperfecta patients) report that patients under 18 were the most likely to receive a treatment of interest, at 32%, against 24.3% across all ages, with bisphosphonates 21.1% and romosozumab 0%. 0.2318 x 0.32 = 0.074174, about 1,268 US children
column12: Judgement on the second share, and it is the row to argue with. The protocol screens on fracture burden, not on Sillence type, and no published distribution of the fracture criterion exists; the measured share of paediatric patients a US physician already treats with an off-label bone agent is the closest observable thing to the same triage, and it is what the bisphosphonate control arm is drawn from. A strict reading of the fracture criterion alone would give less: Yang reports about 40% of patients had a fracture within one year of diagnosis and 33% of paediatric patients with fractures had more than three fractures within a year, and more than three in one year must satisfy three in two years, so 0.40 x 0.33 = 0.132 is a lower bound by construction. The pool is also not cut for ambulatory status or for the COL1A1 or COL1A2 requirement that excludes types V and above, both of which would reduce it. Mixing a Dutch all-age rate with a Swedish paediatric rate is itself a weakness: it implies 23.2% of patients are aged 5 to 17 where the two US claims cohorts read 35.1% and 47.1% under 18, so the age share may be low

a judgement, set well below the published chain on purpose. The published figure, for reference, is the rare-disease cut of the BIO / Informa Pharma Intelligence / QLS Advisors 'Clinical Development Success Rates and Contributing Factors 2011-2020' report, Figure 8b page 14, ahead of a Phase 3 readout: 0.604 Phase 3 to NDA/BLA on 240 transitions and 0.936 NDA/BLA to approval on 172, which is 0.5653. What takes it down is a stated result on the same mechanism in the same disease. Ultragenyx 8-K of 2025-12-29 (0001193125-25-332422, Item 8.01) on setrusumab, the other anti-sclerostin antibody in osteogenesis imperfecta: 'Neither study achieved statistical significance against the primary endpoints of reduction in annualized clinical fracture rate compared to placebo or bisphosphonates, respectively. Both studies achieved the secondary endpoints of improvements in bone mineral density ('BMD') against comparators.' Earlier, in adults, setrusumab also missed: Glorieux FH et al., 'Setrusumab for the treatment of osteogenesis imperfecta: 12-month results from the phase 2b ASTEROID study', J Bone Miner Res 2024;39(9):1215-1228, doi 10.1093/jbmr/zjae112, PMID 39012717, report that the primary endpoint of change in radial trabecular volumetric BMD at month 12 did not reach statistical significance, while several secondary bone measures did. NCT05972551 has three co-primary endpoints, number of clinical fractures at 12 months, number of any fractures at 12 months and change in lumbar spine BMD Z-score; two of the three are the endpoint that has just failed on this mechanism and one is the kind it passed, and 111 participants over 12 months is a small fracture-count trial
column12: Replace this with 0.936, the NDA to approval rate above, if Amgen reports a positive readout at the 2027-05-04 primary completion, or with 0 if it reports a miss. The case for lower: an open-label trial against an active comparator in 111 children is not a design that rescues a fracture endpoint
